title: Select and defend an accessible UI system

bridge.applicationConcept: Design tokens, accessible primitives, interaction states, and component ownership
bridge.analogyLimit: UI libraries can be mixed technically, but mismatched behavior and visual rules still create a poor and inaccessible product.

buildBrief: Compare status cards, tables, dialogs, forms, badges, and feedback states from the curated libraries, then implement one coherent AtlasOps status panel using shared tokens.
incidentBrief: The supplied panel clips at mobile width and exposes a keyboard-inaccessible details control. Repair both while preserving the selected visual direction.

scenario.symptoms: The accessibility and responsive checks report an unnamed control and horizontal overflow.

acceptanceTests: The component comparison records license, ownership, accessibility, bundle, and maintenance tradeoffs
The selected panel uses one token system and works at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths
Keyboard focus and non-color status labels are observable
evidence: Three visual comparisons and selected ADR
Mobile, tablet, desktop, and keyboard captures
predictionQuestions: Which component behavior comes from a primitive and which comes from local styling?
What will happen to the table and actions below 375 pixels?
defenseQuestions: Name the layout, hierarchy, density, rhythm, and feedback decisions.
Explain why the chosen libraries can coexist coherently.
Modify one component state without regenerating the panel.
hints: Inspect semantics and keyboard behavior before visual polish.
Use shared tokens for spacing, radius, color, and focus instead of per-component guesses.
Test the narrowest viewport and zoom before declaring the layout responsive.
